recommended_next_phase: 149O.20L.7O.2F.3 -- FIDO2 Signing-Time Credential Resolution Repair Independent Verification. Narrowly scoped per HSCE-001 v1.2 section 47. Not authorized by this phase; not begun.
summary: Repaired BF-1/BF-2 (149O.20L.7O.2F.1's two Blocking findings) in hatp_signing_ceremony.py by selecting Model B -- durable-registry signer resolution -- over Model A (authenticator rediscovery), after reconstructing signer resolution directly from primary source (HSCE-001 v1.1, HPSE-001 v1.1, HHCE-001 v1.1, hatp_signing_ceremony.py, hatp_fido2_provider.py, hatp_hardware_credentials.py, hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py, hatp_principal_signer_admin.py, hatp_bootstrap.py, human_approval_trusted_provenance.py, and the real pcae hatp sign rollback CLI path), not prior-phase prose. _resolve_signer (BF-1's unconditional provider.credential_identity() call) is replaced by _resolve_deployment_binding_signer, which resolves principal_id/signer_key_id exclusively from this repository's own durable DeploymentBinding (HATPTrustStore.resolve_deployment_authorization, the frozen Layer-1/Layer-2 repository/root match) -- never from the hardware provider. HSCE-001 amended in place to v1.2 (HSCE-REQ-018/024 revised; HSCE-REQ-080..084 added: six-step signer-resolution order, multiple-signer determinism via DeploymentBinding's existing one-per-repository uniqueness, the registry-resolves-identity/hardware-proves-possession authority distinction, an extended TOCTOU recheck covering signer identity, and credential_identity()'s explicit non-required-method disposition). BF-2 required no code change: request_signature() already accepted an explicit signer_key_id and never depended on resident-credential discovery, so enroll_credential()'s non-resident output remains fully valid under Model B -- demonstrated directly, not merely asserted. No provider API change, no enroll_credential() behavior change, no CLI flag added. A full synthetic production-path end-to-end test was added: real enroll_credential() (monkeypatched CTAP2 transport only) -> register_credential (Surface B) -> enroll_principal/enroll_signer (Surface C) -> create_deployment_binding (Surface E) -> the real, injectable sign_rollback_evidence orchestrator with a synthetic hardware touch -> published HATPSignedEvidenceEnvelope; asserts credential_identity() is never called and the provider receives exactly the enrolled credential's signer_key_id. BF-1/BF-2 reproduction tests confirm the original symptoms directly against real source before asserting the repair. Surfaces B-E re-confirmed clean, unmodified (tests/test_hatp_trust_enrollment_capability.py, tests/test_hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py, tests/test_hatp_bootstrap_foundation.py). Security-attack coverage added: multiple active signers (cross-repository isolation), wrong credential, wrong/revoked principal, revoked signer, revoked credential, provider-profile mismatch (both DeploymentBinding-level and HardwareCredentialRecord-level), missing credential, stale-registry-state TOCTOU (new HSCE-REQ-083 recheck), duplicate credential, authenticator-returns-unexpected-credential (verify()'s existing check, unweakened). Regression attribution used the repository's real .venv interpreter (Python 3.9, fido2/cryptography extras) rather than the ambient interpreter, which cannot even collect the FIDO2-dependent test modules; -k hatp and full fast_green suites were each run twice (git-stash-isolated baseline at phase-entry commit 55d7ca8b vs. this phase's tree, then again post-commit against the actual committed diff) and the exact FAILED/ERROR node-ID sets diffed. Every net-new non-passing node ID across all four runs was individually confirmed to be the expected byte-identity/no-production-source-changed/contract-version-frozen self-check family this repository's own project memory already documents as repin-debt for any phase touching a previously-frozen file -- zero undisclosed functional regressions in HATP business logic. HMIC (HATP_MANDATORY_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION_CERTIFICATION_CONTRACT.md) was not amended (not authorized this phase); the exact required future source-scope effect (any future HMIC frozen-source-set baseline spanning hatp_signing_ceremony.py or the HSCE-001 contract file will need its own pinned baseline advanced past this phase's commit) is disclosed in this phase's own report. No real hardware, no real credential/principal/signer enrollment, no real DeploymentBinding, no Dell mutation, no runtime-capability change. Final verdict: FIDO2 SIGNING-TIME CREDENTIAL RESOLUTION REPAIRED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING. BF-1 and BF-2 each marked REPAIRED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING, not self-closed. Recommends 149O.20L.7O.2F.3 (Independent Verification), not authorized, not begun.

validation_results.name: bf1_repro_and_repair
validation_results.result: Production path re-derived from primary source (run_hatp_sign_rollback -> production_sign_rollback_evidence -> sign_rollback_evidence -> _resolve_signer -> provider.credential_identity()) and confirmed unconditional against current source, matching 149O.20L.7O.2F.1's finding exactly. Repair replaces _resolve_signer with _resolve_deployment_binding_signer (HSCE-REQ-080), which never calls credential_identity(); test_bf1_repaired_enrolled_signer_reaches_signing_resolution and the full production-path end-to-end test demonstrate a real enrolled FIDO2 signer now reaches signing-time resolution successfully via the real orchestrator.

validation_results.name: bf2_repro_and_disposition
validation_results.result: enroll_credential()'s ctap2.make_credential(...) call confirmed to still pass no options/rk argument, producing a non-resident credential -- BF-2's original finding reproduced directly. Confirmed moot under Model B: request_signature() already accepted an explicit signer_key_id and never depended on resident-credential discovery; test_bf2_moot_non_resident_credential_remains_fully_valid_for_signing and the end-to-end test demonstrate the non-resident credential remains fully valid for the entire production signing path. No code change to enroll_credential() was needed or made.

validation_results.name: architecture_decision_model_b_selected
validation_results.result: Model A (authenticator rediscovery) and Model B (durable-registry signer resolution) both evaluated against HSCE-001 compatibility, CTAP2 support, multiple-signer behavior, deterministic identity, and the blind-touch-defense requirement. Model B selected: DeploymentBinding already provides a durable, pre-touch-resolvable, structurally-unique-per-repository signer-identity source: Model A was rejected primarily because discovering signer identity via a live hardware call would violate HSCE-REQ-071's blind-touch-defense ordering. Full analysis recorded in HSCE-001 v1.2 section 46.

validation_results.name: hsce_001_amended_v1_1_to_v1_2
validation_results.result: HSCE-REQ-018 table row, HSCE-REQ-024, one HSCE-REQ-047 table cell, and HSCE-REQ-078's count revised; HSCE-REQ-080 through HSCE-REQ-084 added (new sections 46-47). No requirement renumbered or removed. HATP-001, RAE-001, HPSE-001, HHCE-001 confirmed byte-unchanged by this phase.

validation_results.name: multiple_signer_determinism
validation_results.result: DeploymentBinding's existing structural uniqueness (at most one per repository_id, enforced at the writer layer, unamended) fully determines multiple-signer behavior -- no CLI selector added or needed. test_attack_multiple_active_signers_each_repository_resolves_only_its_own independently confirms two fully-enrolled signers on two repositories each resolve only their own.

validation_results.name: authority_distinction_preserved
validation_results.result: request_signature() (unchanged) still performs the sole physical hardware touch, still requires fresh per-operation presence, and its assertion is still independently verified at consumption time against the durable HardwareCredentialRecord's public key -- the DeploymentBinding-resolved signer_key_id is never treated as sufficient authority on its own (HSCE-REQ-082).

validation_results.name: toctou_extended_to_signer_identity
validation_results.result: New HSCE-REQ-083 recheck re-runs the full six-step signer resolution a second time immediately before publication and discards the signed candidate on any (principal_id, signer_key_id) mismatch. test_toctou_signer_identity_rotation_between_preview_and_touch independently confirms a DeploymentBinding rotation landing mid-ceremony is caught, evidence store left empty.
